$comment: The policy archive: federal label requirements as versioned data. Extracted from the eCFR versioner API, digests included so a later re-extraction can detect that a regulation moved. Rules are superseded, never deleted (D27); nothing is enforced without a named approval. Design: design.md §18.
$versioning: contentDigest is sha256 over the canonical JSON of regulations, sourceDocuments and rules, first 16 hex. policySetVersion is a number a person maintains; this is the thing that notices when they forget. The regulations already carry a textDigest so a moved regulation is visible — the set itself had no such tripwire, and an edited set still calling itself version 1 would replay as comparable against rules it was never judged by. policy-set.test.ts pins the pair.

source.$comment: Numeric lists are parsed from the fetched text, never transcribed.

$dating: TWO DIFFERENT DATES, deliberately kept apart. `effectiveFrom` on a rule is the range of SUBMISSION dates it governs — an application filed in 2024 must be judged by the rules in force in 2024, not today's. `extractedFromIssueDate` on a regulation is when this deployment last read the text. Conflating them would let a rule change silently re-judge past decisions.

regulations.heading: Standards of Identity for Distilled Spirits (5.141-5.156)

coverage.$comment: Stated so silence is never read as compliance.
coverage.Distilled spirits: mandatory information, alcohol content, standards of fill; class/type minimum bottling strength extracted as a DRAFT from BAM ch. 4 (pages 1-6, 9-12 of 30 read)
coverage.Malt beverages: not extracted — part 7 read for section titles only. A rule set that half-covers a commodity is worse than one that says it does not.

rules.requirement: The brand name appears on the label.
The class, type, or other designation appears on the label.
Alcohol content is stated as a percentage of alcohol by volume.
Net contents appear on the container.
rules.$note: Absence from artwork is NOT a breach: 5.63(b)(2) permits net contents to be blown, embossed or moulded into the container, which no label image can show. Absent therefore means UNDETERMINED and goes to the agent.

rules.requirement: The statement reads "Alcohol __ percent by volume", "__ percent alcohol by volume", or "Alcohol by volume __ percent"; alcohol may be "alc", percent may be "%", "by" may be "/", volume may be "vol", periods and parentheses optional.
Where degrees of proof are also stated, proof is twice the alcohol by volume.
rules.$note: Answers open question Q8. Needs no application data and no model — the label is checked against itself.

rules.requirement: Net contents are an authorised metric standard of fill for distilled spirits.
rules.$note: Amended by T.D. TTB-200, 90 FR 1876 (10 Jan 2025), which changed the authorised list. The prior list is NOT in this archive, so a submission filed before that date is UNDETERMINED for this rule rather than judged by a list that did not govern it.

rules.requirement: Net contents are an authorised standard of fill for wine.
rules.$note: 4.72(b) permits containers above 3 litres in even litres; this rule stops at 3 litres and a larger container is NOT_APPLICABLE, not a breach.

rules.requirement: The health warning statement appears word for word as prescribed.
rules.$note: Implemented before this archive existed, against config/warning-statement.json. Listed so the set describes everything checked, not only what it added.

rules.requirement: The stated alcohol content is not below the minimum bottling strength for the labelled class or type.

provenance.quote: “Whisky” or “whiskey” is distilled spirits ... and bottled at not less than 40 percent alcohol by volume (80° proof)

rules.$note: Still a DRAFT and still unapproved — the contract requires a person, and nobody has signed it. The blocking dependency is gone: designations now resolve to classes via config/class-type-taxonomy.json.
rules.$openQuestion: Class-level only, and two classes have NO class-level floor at all — cordials and liqueurs (5.150) and distilled spirits specialty products (5.156) — where every stated minimum belongs to a TYPE. A designation resolving to those classes is UNDETERMINED, not satisfied: 'Rock and Rye' has a 24% floor and no class floor to fall back on, so treating a null as 'no limit' would pass any strength.

rules.requirement: Alcohol content is stated as a percentage of alcohol by volume, either as a specific percentage or as a range. Only "alc." and "vol." may abbreviate alcohol and volume, with or without periods; "ABV" is not permitted. The numeral may precede or follow the word.

provenance.quote: Alcoholic content shall be stated in terms of percentage of alcohol by volume, and not otherwise, as provided in either paragraph (b)(1) or (2) of this section: (1) "Alcohol __ % by volume," or similar appropriate phrase; Provided, that if the word "alcohol" and/or "volume" are abbreviated, they shall be shown as "alc." (alc) and/or "vol." (vol), respectively. ... (2) "Alcohol __ % to __ % by volume," or similar appropriate phrase

rules.$draftNote: DRAFT: proposed by a model from 27 CFR 4.36(b) and TTB wine guidance. A model may propose a rule; only a person may enact one (design §18.5a). It is carried here so it can be reviewed against its quote and citation, and it is NOT applied — rulesFor() selects active rules only. To enact it: set status to "active" and record an approval.

rules.requirement: A brand name appears on the label.

provenance.quote: The malt beverage label must include a brand name. If the malt beverage is not sold under a brand name, then the name of the bottler or importer, as applicable, appearing in the name and address statement is treated as the brand name.

rules.$draftNote: DRAFT: proposed by a model from the cited regulation. A model may propose a rule; only a person may enact one (design §18.5a). Not applied — rulesFor() selects active rules only. To enact: set status "active" and record an approval.

rules.requirement: A class, type, or other designation appears on the label.

provenance.quote: Malt beverage containers must bear a label or labels (as defined in § 7.61(a)) containing the following information: ... (2) Class, type, or other designation, in accordance with subpart I of this part

rules.$draftNote: DRAFT: proposed by a model from the cited regulation. A model may propose a rule; only a person may enact one (design §18.5a). Not applied — rulesFor() selects active rules only. To enact: set status "active" and record an approval.

rules.requirement: Net contents appear on the label. Absence is inconclusive: the regulation permits net contents to be blown, embossed or moulded into the container, which no image of a label can show.

provenance.quote: (5) Net contents (which may be blown, embossed, or molded into the container as part of the process of manufacturing the container), in accordance with § 7.70.

rules.$draftNote: DRAFT: proposed by a model from 27 CFR 7.63(a)(5) and 7.70. whenAbsent is "undetermined" for the same reason as the distilled spirits rule — the statement may be moulded into the glass, so an absence from the artwork is not a breach. A model may propose a rule; only a person may enact one (§18.5a).

rules.requirement: When alcohol content is stated, it reads "Alcohol __ percent by volume", "__ percent alcohol by volume", or "Alcohol by volume: __ percent"; alcohol may be "alc", percent may be "%", "by" may be "/", and volume may be "vol".

provenance.quote: The alcohol content statement must be expressed in one of the following formats: (A) "Alcohol percent by volume"; (B) "percent alcohol by volume"; or (C) "Alcohol by volume: percent." ... Alcohol may be abbreviated as "alc"; percent may be represented by the percent symbol "%"; alcohol and volume may be separated by a slash "/" in lieu of the word "by"; and volume may be abbreviated as "vol".

rules.$draftNote: DRAFT: proposed by a model from 27 CFR 7.65(b)(3)-(4). The permitted forms are identical to 27 CFR 5.65 for distilled spirits, so this reuses the abv-statement format rather than introducing a second copy of the same patterns. Only a person may enact it (§18.5a).
